normative_banner: THIS FILE IS NORMATIVE. Any modification — including whitespace, key order, float representation, or comment text — invalidates the canonical fingerprint and the 'VIGÍA-compatible P2' claim. Do not edit by hand for downstream consumption; regenerate from source.
description: Canonical vectors P2 v2.8. 9th audit pass (Kimi + ChatGPT + Grok + Claude + DeepSeek round 2). REFINEMENTS: prng_binding now tiered by compliance level (strict requires bit-identity with NumPy; reference relaxes to statistical equivalence with documented seeding; accelerated permits any seeded PRNG). pe_large_tie_break_complex empirically verified — quantized PE = 0.480709 exact match (pattern distribution: (0,1,2)×200, (1,2,0)×49, (2,0,1)×49). near_equal_symbol_stability note expanded with hex representations of all three symbols. special_float_handling.native_value_rejection_clause adds largest-denormal example (2.2250738585072009e-308) and clarification of the 2^-1022 threshold.

reference_runtime.note: P2 semantics depend on P1 + deterministic algorithms specified herein.

prng_binding.non_numpy_strict: Strict compliance level requires non-NumPy implementations to produce bit-identical output streams to numpy.random.Generator(PCG64(seed)).integers(low, high, size=n, endpoint=False). This is acknowledged to be highly demanding: NumPy's specific 64-bit packing, endianness, and rejection-sampling logic in 'integers()' must be matched exactly. Implementations that cannot meet bit-identity are disqualified from strict compliance.
prng_binding.non_numpy_reference: Reference compliance level relaxes bit-identity to STATISTICAL EQUIVALENCE with documented seeding. Acceptable: any PCG64 family implementation that produces sequences passing standard randomness tests with the same seed semantics. Any divergence from the NumPy reference stream MUST be documented in the compliance manifest, including the specific implementation used and its expected output for the seeds in PRNG-typed vectors.
prng_binding.accelerated: Accelerated compliance: any deterministic seeded PRNG acceptable. Documentation of generator family and seeding required. NOT eligible for 'VIGÍA-compatible P2' claim regardless.
prng_binding.rationale: Without an explicit library binding, 'PCG64' is ambiguous: O'Neill's reference, NumPy's binding, and Boost's implementation produce different output streams from the same seed. P2 pins NumPy as the bit-identity reference for strict compliance, while pragmatically relaxing the requirement to statistical equivalence for reference compliance. This reflects the reality that bit-identity across language ecosystems is generally not achievable for PCG64 even when implementations are mathematically correct.

non_goals: Behavioral classification of humans vs bots
non_goals_note: P2 is a reproducibility contract for entropy mathematics. Any inference beyond distributional properties is outside protocol scope and requires independent forensic validation. Reproducibility is not truth. Determinism is not authority. Mathematical consistency does not imply semantic correctness.

terminology_warnings.description: P2 metrics (entropy, Markov, Lempel-Ziv, permutation entropy) are distributional descriptors. They are NOT detectors of: AI-generated content, human authorship, deception, manipulation, intent, or authenticity. Names of mathematical quantities must not be reified into ontological categories.
terminology_warnings.rationale: Distributional properties of a signal do not encode the ontological status of its producer. A high-entropy sequence is not 'more human' and a low-entropy sequence is not 'more synthetic'. Any such mapping requires a calibrated, dataset-specific, externally validated decision layer that is OUTSIDE P2 scope.
terminology_warnings.revocation_clause: Any build whose documentation, UI labels, CLI output, API field names, or marketing material uses any phrase from prohibited_interpretive_phrasings AUTOMATICALLY FORFEITS the right to claim 'VIGÍA-compatible P2', regardless of vector passage. This is non-negotiable and applies retroactively to any prior claim.
terminology_warnings.enforcement_note: Validators MAY scan implementation strings for prohibited phrasings as a best-effort check, but the revocation clause is normative regardless of automated enforcement.

interpretation_safeguards.description: Even with terminology_warnings, the ecosystem will attempt to reinterpret entropy metrics as ontological signals (high entropy → human, low entropy → AI). This block documents the failure modes of that reinterpretation and the counterexamples implementations SHOULD include in user-facing documentation.

naive_reinterpretation_failure_modes.naive_claim: High Shannon entropy indicates human authorship
examples: Form-filling, structured templates, repetitive professional writing
Stylistically constrained genres (legal, medical, technical reports)
Speech-to-text under quiet conditions with predictable phrasing

naive_reinterpretation_failure_modes.naive_claim: Low Shannon entropy indicates synthetic/AI authorship
examples: Adversarially-trained generators optimized for distributional naturalness
Models with explicit entropy regularization toward natural-text targets

naive_reinterpretation_failure_modes.naive_claim: Low Lempel-Ziv complexity indicates non-natural origin
naive_reinterpretation_failure_modes.counterexample_category: Natural sources of low LZ complexity
examples: Sensor data in quiescent physical systems

naive_reinterpretation_failure_modes.counterexample_category: Deterministic chaotic systems producing high PE
examples: Logistic map at chaotic parameter regimes
Deterministic PRNG output (high PE despite full determinism)
Lorenz attractor trajectories at small embedding dimensions

interpretation_safeguards.documentation_requirement: Implementations claiming VIGÍA-compatible P2 SHOULD include at least one counterexample from each REINT-NN category in any user-facing material that displays P2 metric values. This is recommended, not normative, but strongly encouraged.
interpretation_safeguards.rationale_for_inclusion: P2's mathematical core cannot prevent semantic misuse downstream. The most honest available defense is to make the failure modes legible alongside the metrics themselves. Counterexamples in documentation reduce — but do not eliminate — the risk of ecosystem reinterpretation.

discretization_policy.description: P2 operates on discrete symbols under exact float64 equality. Continuous signals (audio, sensor data, network telemetry, DSP output) MUST be discretized before P2 metrics are applied. P2 does NOT define the discretization step.
in_scope: Mathematics of discrete symbol sequences once discretization is fixed
Reproducibility of metric output given identical discrete input
Rejection of NaN, Inf, denormals at metric ingress
out_of_scope: Choice of bin width, codebook, or quantizer for continuous data
ADC quantization, jitter compensation, DSP normalization
Codec artifacts, GPU kernel rounding, parser float drift
Symbolic explosion induced by floating-point noise in upstream pipelines
discretization_policy.upstream_risk_acknowledgment: Real-world signals are subject to noise, jitter, codec artifacts, and parser drift that can artificially inflate the symbol space under exact-equality symbolization. P2 is mathematically consistent but is NOT, by itself, forensically robust against this upstream risk. Implementations applying P2 to continuous data MUST document their discretization step in the chain-of-custody manifest.
discretization_policy.chain_of_custody_requirement: Any P2 application to non-natively-discrete data MUST record the discretization function, its parameters, and its provenance in the chain_of_custody.processing_manifest. Failure to do so invalidates forensic reproducibility claims even if P2 vectors pass.
discretization_policy.future_work: A formal upstream discretization standard is a candidate for P3 (tracked as P3-01 in governance.future_work_p3). The VIGÍA AI Collective explicitly endorses ChatGPT's diagnosis that discretization is plausibly the 'real P3' rather than a side concern: two pipelines applying different discretizers to the same physical phenomenon currently produce 'reproducible mathematical truths over different representations of the same underlying signal', which is a known unresolved tension. P2 deliberately delegates this to the implementer to keep the mathematical core freezable; P3 is expected to close the gap.

canonicalization.signed_zero_symbolization: +0.0 and -0.0 MUST map to same symbol per IEEE-754 equality
canonicalization.rounding_reference: IEEE-754 round-half-to-even via Python decimal module
canonicalization.rounding_note: Uses Decimal.quantize() with explicit context. Eliminates platform-dependent C library round() divergence.

serialization_layers.description: Tres capas separadas: transport, serialization, semantic.

transport_layer.note: Standard JSON per RFC 8259. No semantic extensions at this layer.

rules.float_serialization_semantic: Shortest round-trip decimal representation preserving IEEE-754 float64

serialization_layer.note: Semantic definition is PRIMARY. CPython reference is SECONDARY and INFORMATIVE.

semantic_layer.parser_requirement: Test runner must interpret semantic-layer tokens per input_encoding specification, not as literal transport-layer dict values

hash_computation.description: SHA-256 computed over exact UTF-8 bytes of canonical_vectors_p2.json
hash_computation.validator_requirement: Validator MUST compute SHA-256 of the canonical_vectors file at runtime and compare against canonical_vectors_p2.sha256
hash_computation.validator_note: Hash verification prevents tampering and ensures the exact vectors used for validation match the signed specification.

backend_equivalence.reduction_order_note: Parallel reductions may accumulate in different order. Result must still match after canonical quantization.
backend_equivalence.accumulator_dtype_note: No float32, no tensor cores, no mixed precision. float64 IEEE-754 required for all intermediate accumulations.
backend_equivalence.maximum_nondeterminism_note: After canonical quantization, all backends must produce identical results. Zero tolerance post-quantization.
backend_equivalence.backend_equivalence_note: Not bit-identical. Identical after canonical decimal quantization.

invariants.comparison_rule: quantize(actual, 6) == quantize(expected, 6) for scalars; structural equality for objects; raises for negative tests
invariants.p1_prerequisite: Build MUST pass P1 canonical vectors before P2 validation

symbolization_policy.description: Explicit policy for converting raw values into discrete symbols.
symbolization_policy.definition: Two values a, b are the same symbol iff a == b under IEEE-754 float64 equality
symbolization_policy.signed_zero_semantic: +0.0 and -0.0 MUST map to same symbol (IEEE-754 equality returns True)
symbolization_policy.canonicalization_before_symbolization_no: Values are symbolized BEFORE quantization. 1.0000000001 and 1.0 are DIFFERENT symbols.
symbolization_policy.hash_based_symbolization_note: No hashing, no bucketing, no binning for discrete entropy functions.
symbolization_policy.continuous_data_note: For continuous data, user must discretize externally. P2 does not provide automatic binning.

implications.entropy_shannon: Operates on exact float64 equality histogram
implications.entropy_normalized: Operates on exact float64 equality histogram
implications.entropy_rate: Operates on exact float64 equality of pairs
implications.markov_order_k: Operates on exact float64 equality of symbols
implications.lempel_ziv: Operates on exact equality of discrete symbols
implications.permutation_entropy: Operates on exact float64 comparison for rank ordering

pair_encoding_definition.description: Formalized encoding of pairs (a, b) into a unique uint64 token.
pair_encoding_definition.endianness_note: a occupies bits [63:32], b occupies bits [31:0]. Bit order is semantic, not platform-dependent.
pair_encoding_definition.collision_free_proof: For uint32 a,b, mapping (a,b) -> (a<<32)|b is bijective into uint64. No collisions possible.
pair_encoding_definition.coercion_policy_note: No implicit type conversion. Inputs must be explicitly validated as uint32 before packing.

requirements: All 22 P2 vectors + all P1 vectors

requirements: All 22 P2 vectors + all P1 vectors
Any backend permitted (GPU, SIMD, custom kernels)
float32/float16 permitted with documented precision loss
Must pass documented subset of P2 vectors
CANNOT claim 'VIGÍA-compatible P2' without explicit deviation documentation

shannon_entropy_definition.self_containment_note: Inherited semantically from P1. Inlined here so P2 reviewers do not need P1 in-hand.
shannon_entropy_definition.alphabet_construction: Set of distinct symbols extracted from the input via exact_equality symbolization (per symbolization_policy). No binning, no hashing.

entropy_normalized_definition.self_containment_note: Inherited semantically from P1. Inlined here for self-containment.
entropy_normalized_definition.description: Shannon entropy normalized by the maximum possible entropy for the alphabet size.

entropy_rate_definition.self_containment_note: Inherited semantically from P1. Inlined here for self-containment.
entropy_rate_definition.description: Shannon entropy computed over the distribution of pairs (a, b) tokenized via pair_encoding into uint64 tokens. Used for evaluating sequence-pair distributions, not just single-symbol distributions.
entropy_rate_definition.normalized_formula: H_rate / log2(|distinct pair tokens|) when |distinct pair tokens| > 1; 0 otherwise
entropy_rate_definition.pair_construction: Adjacent non-overlapping pairs of input symbols, encoded via pair_encoding_definition

markov_order_k_definition.formula: H_k = -sum_{w in contexts} P(w) * sum_{s in symbols} P(s|w) * log2(P(s|w))
markov_order_k_definition.empty_context: k=0 uses empty tuple () as sole context
markov_order_k_definition.smoothing_note: MLE puro. No Laplace, no Kneser-Ney, no add-epsilon, no Dirichlet.

lempel_ziv_definition.description: Counts the number of unique subsequences in the LZ76 factorization.
lempel_ziv_definition.pseudocode:
INPUT:  sequence S[0..n-1] of discrete symbols
OUTPUT: integer c = number of unique components

1. IF n == 0: RETURN 0
2. c ← 1; u ← 1; v ← 1; vmax ← 1; i ← 0
3. WHILE u + v <= n:
4.     IF S[i + v - 1] == S[u + v - 1]: v ← v + 1
5.     ELSE:
6.         vmax ← max(v, vmax); i ← i + 1
7.         IF i == u: c ← c + 1; u ← u + vmax; v ← 1; i ← 0; vmax ← 1
8.         ELSE: v ← 1
9. IF v != 1: c ← c + 1
10. RETURN c
lempel_ziv_definition.pseudocode_worked_examples_ref: See reference_factorization_semantics.reference_examples below for two fully worked factorizations ([1,2,1,2,1,2] → 3 factors; [1,2,3,...] period-3 → 4 factors). Implementations MUST reproduce these factorizations exactly.
lempel_ziv_definition.novelty_criterion: Longest prefix of S[u..] appearing in S[0..u-1]
lempel_ziv_definition.complexity_note: Implementation-dependent. Naive implementations may exhibit O(n²) worst-case. Optimized suffix-tree implementations may achieve O(n). Reference pseudocode is O(n²) worst-case.
lempel_ziv_definition.complexity_reference: Lempel & Ziv (1976) proved upper bound; practical complexity depends on implementation strategy
lempel_ziv_definition.normalization_note: Converges to 1.0 for random, 0.0 for periodic
lempel_ziv_definition.continuous_data: must be discretized before LZ application

reference_factorization_semantics.factor_boundary_rule: Each factor is the shortest prefix of the unprocessed suffix that has NOT appeared as a contiguous substring in the processed prefix
reference_factorization_semantics.eof_semantics: If trailing suffix cannot form a new factor, it is added as final factor (c += 1)

permutation_entropy_definition.description: Entropy of ordinal patterns. Invariant under monotonic transformations.
permutation_entropy_definition.precondition_violation: raise ValueError('Sequence too short for d={d}, tau={tau}. Required: n >= d*tau')
permutation_entropy_definition.pattern_extraction: For each window of length d with delay tau, compute rank permutation
permutation_entropy_definition.tie_breaking: stable_sort_by_time_index: earlier index wins on equality
permutation_entropy_definition.tie_breaking_note: Critical for cross-backend equivalence. Two equal values → earlier position gets lower rank.
permutation_entropy_definition.normalization: Divided by log2(d!) to bound in [0, 1]

abstention_policy_definition.description: Mathematical formalization of abstention as a protocol property.

abstention_zone.range_notation: Open interval: parentheses '()' EXCLUDE the endpoints. A score of exactly 0.15 maps to LOW_VARIABILITY; a score of exactly 0.85 maps to HIGH_VARIABILITY. Only scores STRICTLY between 0.15 and 0.85 trigger ABSTAIN.
abstention_zone.description: Scores in this range trigger ABSTAIN
abstention_zone.mathematical_semantic: Insufficient distributional evidence for protocol-level classification
abstention_zone.zone_assignment_rule: score <= 0.15 → LOW_VARIABILITY; score >= 0.85 → HIGH_VARIABILITY; 0.15 < score < 0.85 → ABSTAIN. Endpoints are deliberately assigned to LOW/HIGH (not ABSTAIN) to maintain mutual exclusivity of the three zones.

abstention_policy_definition.calibration_status_note: The 0.15 / 0.85 thresholds are placeholders chosen for symmetry around the unit interval. They are NOT empirically calibrated against forensic datasets. Mathematical protocol freeze does NOT freeze these thresholds.
abstention_policy_definition.calibration_freeze_requirement: Before P2 final freeze, thresholds MUST be validated against at least one published forensic corpus with documented sensitivity/specificity reporting. Until then, thresholds are advisory and any production deployment MUST document threshold provenance.
abstention_policy_definition.note: Protocol invariants describing distributional properties, not forensic conclusions. Forensic interpretation is outside P2 scope.

known_adversarial_gaps.description: Honest enumeration of adversarial scenarios NOT yet covered by canonical vectors. Each gap has a stable short ID (GAP-NN) for issue tracking and cross-referencing. These are documented as future-work to prevent overclaiming P2 robustness.
known_adversarial_gaps.id_scheme: GAP-NN stable identifiers. IDs are append-only; once assigned, an ID is never reused or renumbered.

gaps.name: entropy_inflation_attack
gaps.description: Adversary injects low-rate uniform noise to push distributional metrics toward the high-variability zone without altering semantic content.

gaps.name: symbolic_explosion_attack
gaps.description: Adversary exploits exact-equality symbolization by introducing sub-ULP float perturbations that artificially expand the symbol space and inflate Shannon entropy.

gaps.name: calibration_drift
gaps.description: Threshold semantics may degrade over time as upstream data distributions shift. P2 does not currently specify drift-detection or recalibration cadence.

gaps.name: backend_divergence_under_stress
gaps.description: Parallel reductions under high core count and mixed workloads may produce post-quantization equivalence empirically but with margins that erode under adversarial input shapes.

gaps.name: heterogeneous_hardware_reproducibility
gaps.description: Cross-vendor GPU determinism (NVIDIA vs AMD vs Apple Silicon) has not been empirically validated for all P2 vectors at the reference compliance level.

gaps.name: false_structure_induction
gaps.description: Pathological inputs that induce coincidentally low LZ complexity or low permutation entropy without genuine structural regularity (e.g., aliasing artifacts at specific window sizes).

gaps.name: dataset_leakage_in_calibration
gaps.description: If abstention thresholds are calibrated on a corpus that overlaps with deployment data, sensitivity/specificity figures will be optimistically biased.

gaps.name: upstream_discretization_attack
gaps.description: Adversary controls the discretization step (out of P2 scope) to push downstream P2 outputs into desired zones. P2 cannot defend against this without chain-of-custody attestation of the discretizer.

gaps.name: tie_break_exploitation
gaps.description: Permutation entropy's stable-sort tie-break is deterministic but adversarially exploitable by constructing inputs with many equal values to force specific permutation distributions.

gaps.name: lz_period_aliasing
gaps.description: LZ76 normalization c(n) / (n / log2(n)) is asymptotic. For short sequences with periods near sqrt(n), normalized scores may misrepresent true compressibility.

known_adversarial_gaps.future_work_commitment: Each gap above is a candidate target for the P2-to-final-freeze validation campaign. P3 may introduce dedicated vectors for the gaps that mature into stable test scenarios. Issues SHOULD reference gaps by GAP-NN identifier.

chain_of_custody_definition.description: Mecanismo de trazabilidad para evidencia procesada por VIGÍA.

output_attestation.deterministic_output_hash: SHA-256 of output given evidence + protocol
output_attestation.reproducibility_claim: Same evidence + same protocol = same output

special_float_handling.description: Protocol-layer synthetic tokens for special float values
special_float_handling.note: These are NOT native JSON numeric literals. They require protocol-aware parser interpretation.
special_float_handling.parser_requirement: Test runner must interpret these wrappers per input_encoding specification, not as literal dict values
special_float_handling.native_value_rejection_clause: Implementations MUST reject ANY native float64 value matching a special-float predicate, not only the synthetic protocol-layer tokens. Concretely: math.isnan(x) → reject; math.isinf(x) → reject; (x != 0 and abs(x) < 2^-1022) → reject as denormal. The threshold 2^-1022 ≈ 2.2250738585072014e-308 is the smallest positive NORMAL float64; any nonzero value with strictly smaller absolute value is a denormal (subnormal). Examples of native values that MUST be rejected: float('nan'), float('inf'), -float('inf'), 5e-324 (smallest positive denormal), -5e-324, 2.2250738585072009e-308 (largest positive denormal, immediately below the normal range), -2.2250738585072009e-308. Rejection MUST raise ValueError. The synthetic token form is for protocol-test plumbing; the native rejection clause is what implementations actually enforce on user input.

vectors.note: Simple periodic sequence → few unique components. Input length n=900, period=3.

vectors.name: lz_random_high
vectors.description: Normalized LZC over a pseudo-random sequence. High complexity.
vectors.note: Random sequence → maximum unique components → LZC converges to 1.0.

expected.note: Raw factorization validates parsing semantics, not just score

vectors.description: Verification of raw LZ factorization. Validates internal parsing.
vectors.note: Dos implementaciones pueden producir mismo score con parsing distinto. Este vector detecta eso.

vectors.name: lz_raw_factorization_periodic

expected.note: Periodic sequence produces predictable factorization pattern

vectors.description: LZ factorization of a periodic sequence. Predictable factor pattern.
vectors.note: Validates that incremental parsing matches the exact reference pseudocode.

vectors.name: pe_periodic_sin
vectors.description: PE de sinusoide. Patrones ordinales parcialmente predecibles.
vectors.note: Sinusoide produce patrones ordinales no uniformes.

vectors.name: pe_monotonic_zero
vectors.description: PE of a monotonic sequence. A single ordinal pattern.
vectors.note: Strictly increasing sequence → only pattern (0,1,2) → PE = 0.0.

vectors.name: pe_random_high
vectors.description: PE of a uniform random sequence. Equiprobable ordinal patterns.
vectors.note: Aleatorio uniforme → 3! = 6 patrones equiprobables → PE ≈ 1.0.

vectors.name: pe_tie_break_stability
vectors.description: PE with consecutive repeated values forcing tie-breaking. Verifies stable sort by time index.
vectors.note: All 4 windows of length 3 are either (1,1,1) or (1,1,2) or (1,2,2) or (2,2,2); each maps to the single pattern (0,1,2) under stable sort. PE = 0.0. (Earlier v2.5 used [1,1,2,2,1,2] which DeepSeek correctly identified as yielding PE ≈ 0.580279, not 0.0. Fixed in v2.7.)

vectors.name: pe_large_tie_break_complex
vectors.description: Large-scale PE with complex tie-breaking. 300 elements, multiple ties.
vectors.note: Sequence [1,1,2,2,3,3]*50 produces 3 cyclic patterns under stable sort. PE = 0.480709.

vectors.name: abstention_boundary_middle
vectors.description: Score in the abstention zone. Must trigger ABSTAIN per protocol.
vectors.note: 9:1 ratio → H_norm ≈ 0.47. The expected gte/lte values [0.15, 0.85] assert the COMPUTED ENTROPY lies in that closed range for this specific input; this is the test-level range assertion. It does NOT redefine the abstention zone, which is the OPEN interval (0.15, 0.85) per abstention_zone.range_notation. Endpoints belong to LOW/HIGH, not ABSTAIN.

vectors.name: abstention_boundary_low
vectors.description: Score <= epsilon_reject (0.15). Low variability classification permitted.
vectors.note: Entropy 0.0 <= 0.15 → low_variability classification permitted.

vectors.name: abstention_boundary_high
vectors.description: Score >= epsilon_accept (0.85). High variability classification permitted.
vectors.note: Entropy 1.0 >= 0.85 → high_variability classification permitted.

vectors.name: reject_denormal
vectors.description: Rejection of denormals (subnormals). Violates the float64 invariant.
vectors.note: Denormals can cause underflow. P2 rejects them explicitly.

vectors.name: reject_nan_inf_combined
vectors.description: Combined rejection of NaN and Inf in the same sequence.
vectors.note: Any presence of NaN or Inf in the sequence must be rejected with ValueError.

vectors.name: large_scale_stability
vectors.description: Large-scale stability: 100k elements, range 2^20. Verifies numerical stability at scale.
vectors.note: Maximum entropy ≈ log2(2^20) = 20.0. float64 accumulator mandatory.

vectors.name: pair_fuzz_max_uint32
vectors.description: Fuzzing of pair encoding with uint32 maxima.
vectors.note: (2^32-1 << 32) | (2^32-1) = 18446744073709551615 = 2^64-1. Token must equal uint64 maximum and fit in uint64.

vectors.name: near_equal_symbol_stability
vectors.description: Near-equal values with symbol stability. Verifies exact symbolization.
vectors.note: Three equiprobable distinct float64 symbols (1.0, 1.000000000000001, 1.000000000000002) yield H = log2(3) = 1.584963. Hex representations: 1.0 → 0x1.0000000000000p+0; 1.000000000000001 → 0x1.0000000000005p+0; 1.000000000000002 → 0x1.0000000000009p+0. The three are pairwise distinct under IEEE-754 float64 equality, hence symbolized as three different symbols per the exact_equality rule. The choice of literal decimal values (rather than something like 1.0 + 1e-15) is deliberate: implementations parsing the JSON via standard libraries will recover these exact bit patterns from the decimal literals, so the test is robust across language ecosystems.

vectors.name: entropy_rate_pairs_intermediate
vectors.description: Entropy rate with 2 unique pairs in uniform distribution. H = log2(2) = 1.0, normalized = 1.0.

validation_rules.p1_prerequisite: Build MUST pass P1 canonical vectors before P2 validation

future_work_p3.description: Scope deliberately excluded from P2. P3 is the candidate protocol for these capabilities. Listed here so that P2 freeze decisions are made with explicit awareness of what P2 is NOT trying to be.

items.name: formal_upstream_discretization_standard
items.description: Standardized discretization functions with reproducibility contracts. Today P2 delegates discretization to the implementer; P3 candidate work is to provide a canonical set with calibrated parameters per data modality. Two pipelines applying different discretizers to the same phenomenon currently produce 'reproducible mathematical truths over different representations' — this is philosophically delicate and warrants its own protocol layer.

items.name: score_fusion_and_weighting
items.description: P2 produces individual distributional measurements. It does not specify how to combine entropy + LZ + Markov + PE into a single decision or evidence object. Fusion strategies (weighted sums, Bayesian aggregation, Dempster-Shafer combination) are out of P2 scope. P3 candidate work.

items.name: uncertainty_propagation
items.description: P2 reports point estimates. Confidence intervals, credible intervals, bootstrap variance estimates, and uncertainty propagation through fusion are P3 candidates.

items.name: calibration_protocol
items.description: A formal protocol for empirical calibration of abstention thresholds against forensic corpora, including sensitivity/specificity reporting, calibration drift monitoring, and recalibration cadence. Currently flagged in abstention_policy_definition.calibration_status.

items.name: peircean_inference_closure
items.description: Today P2 measures. It does not yet reason. Closing the Peircean loop (abduction → deduction → induction over P2 measurements) is the candidate semantic layer above P2. Out of scope for current freeze.

future_work_p3.rationale: P2 is deliberately scoped as a mathematical reproducibility contract. Composition, fusion, uncertainty, and inference belong at a higher layer. Keeping P2 minimal is what makes it freezable; the cost is that P2 alone is not a forensic system, it is forensic infrastructure.
